gloss: To look ahead and look back; to consider all aspects before making a decision.
teaser: Ever felt torn between past decisions and future possibilities? This idiom captures that struggle.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever felt torn between past decisions and future possibilities? This idiom captures that struggle.[break 1s]The phrase is: 瞻前顾后 (zhān qián gù hòu).[break 0.5s]瞻 (zhān) - to look at; to gaze at [break 0.5s]前 (qián) - front; ahead [break 0.5s]顾 (gù) - to look back; to consider [break 0.5s]后 (hòu) - back; behind [break 1s]So, 瞻前顾后 literally means 'to look ahead and look back' and figuratively refers to considering all aspects before making a decision.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]In ancient times, a wise strategist advised a king to always assess both the past and future when making plans. He emphasized that understanding previous mistakes could prevent future failures. Thus, the phrase evolved to remind people to look both ways before proceeding in life.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 在做决定之前，我总是瞻前顾后。 [break 1s]Before making a decision, I always look ahead and look back. [break 1s]Example 2: 她在选择职业时瞻前顾后，考虑了很多因素。 [break 1s]She looked ahead and looked back when choosing her career, considering many factors. [break 1s]Example 3: 在投资之前，我们应该瞻前顾后，仔细分析市场。 [break 1s]Before investing, we should look ahead and look back, carefully analyzing the market. [break 1s]So, 瞻前顾后 means to consider all aspects before making a decision. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
